title: Effect of a New Income on the Premium Band and the Cost-Sharing Cap
content:
## Effect of a new income on the premium band and the cost-sharing cap

**Clause.** For a Medicaid Managed Care Membership, a new income on the state enrollment file sets the premium band from the first coverage month billed after the update and sets the cost-sharing cap from the first cap period that starts after the update; periods and months already started keep the income on file at their start. While a continuous eligibility period is running, a new income may move the premium to a lower band but never to a higher one; a higher band waits until the next renewal approval. Members must report income changes within the category's change report days, but a late report never creates a retroactive premium or copay charge.

### When the new income applies

| Item | First item to use the new income | Items already started |
|---|---|---|
| Premium band | First coverage month billed after the update | Keep the income on file at their start |
| Cost-sharing cap | First cap period that starts after the update | Keep the income on file at their start |

### Band movement

| Continuous eligibility period | New income points to a lower band | New income points to a higher band |
|---|---|---|
| Running | May move to the lower band | Stays in the current band until the next renewal approval |
| Not running | Band follows the new income | Band follows the new income |

### Hypothetical cases

Hypothetical inputs only:

- The state file updates the income on 14 May. The next coverage month billed after the update takes the band the new income sets; a cap period that had already started before 14 May keeps the income that was on file at its start, and the next cap period to start uses the new income.
- A child's continuous eligibility period is running and the new income would place the family in a higher band. The premium stays in the current band until the next renewal approval.
- A family reports an income change after the change report days have passed. The late report does not create any retroactive premium or copay charge.
